title: History, correction and deletion
brief: Represent agreements, corrections and deletion without confusing today’s state with history.
outcomes: Distinguish effective time from recorded time
Trace a correction or deletion through dependent and external records
entry: Keys, references, agreed prices and typed time.

heading.title: An agreement and a current value
heading.brief: Change P7’s catalogue price after order 103 while its unit_price remains 20.00; distinguish stored evidence from recomputation.

heading.title: When a fact applied
heading.brief: Use a dated price correction to separate effective periods from when staff learnt the correction; make interval boundaries explicit.

heading.title: Correction without erasure
heading.brief: Compare current-row replacement, version history and events by the questions each can answer; avoid promising an audit trail from timestamps alone.

heading.title: Deletion and retention
heading.brief: Trace a customer erasure through orders, history, replicas, exports and backups; explain domain retention decisions without prescribing legal policy.

nested_article.title: Table partitioning and data lifecycle
nested_article.brief: Use table partitions for a useful pruning or lifecycle boundary without assuming they distribute work.
outcomes: Account for uniqueness, references and safe retention
nested_article.entry: Typed time, indexes and history requirements.
